## Overview

Adds shared FP8/INT8 SSM checkpoints to FlashInfer ReplaySSM.
PR #55688 merged into `main` at `750cad1973f037fe00116cbf58cd3b3bd8701cd4`.
This branch now uses `main` at `4527515cd705db206ae927cf5acef506abc64bdd`. The separate CuTeDSL implementation remains in draft #65660.

Review the [shared-only comparison](https://github.com/askliar/vllm/compare/4527515cd705db206ae927cf5acef506abc64bdd...911ffe1d78cbb31b618a87fd2911fa6b57fd4597).
This PR no longer includes the unmerged parent history.

```text
BF16 inputs → shared FP8/INT8 checkpoint + FP32 row scales → FlashInfer SSU
```

## Claims

- `--replayssm-state-dtype fp8|int8` selects a shared quantized checkpoint. The default `auto` path retains floating-point state.
- Prefill, cache copying, and prefix materialization preserve each checkpoint with its FP32 scales.
- Existing stochastic-rounding controls apply to shared decode writes. Prefill encoding uses nearest rounding.
- This layer adds no separate checkpoint mode or vendored CuTeDSL kernels.

## Measured results

**Historical measurements at `927e98f31cc9f6bfafdb976ee2884b111446f371`, before this branch update.**
The 21 measurements and model evaluations below were not repeated on `911ffe1d78cbb31b618a87fd2911fa6b57fd4597`.
They describe the measured source, not fresh GPU validation of the updated branch.

**Super 3 NVFP4, one GB300, TP1, V2, CUDA graphs, BF16 operands, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, and no prefix caching.**
Each cell contains one measured run. There are no repetitions or ABBA averages.
MTP uses natural acceptance and normal expert routing.
SR5 means five Philox rounds for stochastic rounding of decode checkpoint stores. Quantized prefill uses nearest rounding.

### Shared ReplaySSM ON output TPS

Standard decoding generates 1,000 tokens per request. Natural MTP3 generates 256 tokens per GSM8K question.
Output TPS includes prefill and complete generation.

| Workload | Batch | FP32, SR off | BF16, SR off | FP16 SR5 | FP8 SR5, raw† | INT8 SR5 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Natural MTP3 | 512 | 24,480.3667 | 27,466.0912 | 26,190.7631 | 16,610.3360† | 24,049.9214 |
| Natural MTP3 | 256 | 19,473.3360 | 21,158.0705 | 20,500.9949 | 12,599.4779† | 19,387.1414 |
| Standard decoding | 256 | 16,076.7799 | 19,693.5126 | 13,041.0746 | 12,114.0366† | 12,003.8558 |

**† FP8 SR5 failed the quality comparison. All marked TPS values and ratios are raw generation measurements.**
The full-test score was **61.41%**, versus **90.90%** for FP32.

### FP32 ReplaySSM OFF references

Each ratio divides ON output TPS by the same workload's FP32 OFF output TPS.
FP32 ON/OFF compares ReplaySSM at the same checkpoint precision with SR disabled.
Other columns combine ReplaySSM and checkpoint precision changes. FP16, FP8, and INT8 columns also include SR5 costs.

| Workload | Batch | FP32 OFF TPS | FP32 ON/OFF | BF16 ON/OFF | FP16 SR5 ON/OFF | FP8 SR5 ON/OFF, raw† | INT8 SR5 ON/OFF |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Natural MTP3 | 512 | 11,348.3404 | 2.1572× | 2.4203× | 2.3079× | 1.4637×† | 2.1192× |
| Natural MTP3 | 256 | 10,090.3307 | 1.9299× | 2.0969× | 2.0317× | 1.2487×† | 1.9214× |
| Standard decoding | 256 | 12,259.1275 | 1.3114× | 1.6064× | 1.0638× | 0.9882×† | 0.9792× |

All original 18 runs completed with zero preemptions on the same timed GPU.
Requested batch size can exceed simultaneous decoding. The OFF MTP runs reached peak concurrency 217 and 216 at batches 256 and 512.
These single-run ratios do not estimate measurement variability.

### INT8 without stochastic rounding

Three subsequent measurements used shared INT8 with SR disabled and zero Philox rounds.
These runs used the same physical GB300, driver, power limit, runtime, source, model, dataset, and workload settings as the original 18 runs.
Prefill conversion remained unchanged. Each workload had one observation, without ABBA or repeated-run averaging.

| Workload | Batch | BF16, SR off TPS | INT8 SR5 TPS | INT8, SR off TPS | Change versus INT8 SR5 | Change versus BF16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Standard decoding | 256 | 19,693.5126 | 12,003.8558 | 17,851.3474 | +48.71% | -9.35% |
| Natural MTP3 | 256 | 21,158.0705 | 19,387.1414 | 18,778.4258 | -3.14% | -11.25% |
| Natural MTP3 | 512 | 27,466.0912 | 24,049.9214 | 25,517.4337 | +6.10% | -7.09% |

All three runs completed with zero preemptions. BF16 retained the highest measured output TPS in each workload.
INT8 without SR scored **1190/1319 (90.22%)** on GSM8K, with **zero invalid answers** and **21 truncated outputs**.
INT8 SR5 scored 1198/1319 (90.83%). These single observations do not establish performance variability or quality parity.

### Full-test GSM8K accuracy

Each MTP3 batch-256 ON process evaluated all 1,319 test questions after its throughput interval.
Accuracy uses zero-shot chat questions, thinking disabled, temperature zero, EOS enabled, and a 1,024-token limit.
The scorer removes commas and extracts the last integer digit run, following the [repository GSM8K rule](https://github.com/askliar/vllm/blob/927e98f31cc9f6bfafdb976ee2884b111446f371/tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py).
Truncated, unparseable, corrupted, or unfinished outputs count as incorrect. Invalid and truncated counts can overlap.

| Checkpoint | Correct/1,319 | Accuracy | Invalid answers | Truncated outputs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FP32, SR off | 1199/1319 | 90.90% | 0 | 12 |
| BF16, SR off | 1202/1319 | 91.13% | 0 | 14 |
| FP16 SR5 | 1203/1319 | 91.21% | 0 | 16 |
| FP8 SR5 — quality failed | 810/1319 | 61.41% | 392 | 445 |
| INT8 SR5 | 1198/1319 | 90.83% | 0 | 17 |
| INT8, SR off (subsequent run) | 1190/1319 | 90.22% | 0 | 21 |

These results do not establish quality parity or accuracy under other evaluation protocols.

### FP8 diagnosis

The native SM103a conversion probe passed 2,112 packed comparisons with zero hardware/software mismatches.
The representable-value oracle passed. Sixteen graph replays produced sixteen unique seeds.
This checks selected conversion inputs and the default PyTorch graph RNG.
The probe does not check the full vLLM graph or SSM state arithmetic.

Full-model FP8 without stochastic rounding scored **926/1319 (70.20%)**, with **265 invalid answers** and **308 truncated outputs**.
The quality drop persists with SR disabled. The root cause remains unresolved.

It is not aggregate decode-only TPS over a fixed interval with all requests decoding.
Mean AL is the natural mean acceptance length, including the verifier token.
All FP8 TPS values below are raw measurements from the configuration that failed the quality comparison.

| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| Standard decoding | 256 | ON | BF16 | 19,693.5126 | 78.0573 | 256 | — | 0 |
| Standard decoding | 256 | ON | FP16 SR5 | 13,041.0746 | 51.4175 | 256 | — | 0 |
| Standard decoding | 256 | ON | FP8 SR5 — raw, quality failed† | 12,114.0366† | 47.7935† | 256 | — | 0 |
| Standard decoding | 256 | ON | INT8 SR5 | 12,003.8558 | 47.3444 | 256 | — | 0 |
| Natural MTP3 | 256 | ON | FP32 | 19,473.3360 | 96.7650 | 256 | 3.3905 | 0 |
| Natural MTP3 | 256 | ON | BF16 | 21,158.0705 | 107.4854 | 256 | 3.4065 | 0 |
| Natural MTP3 | 256 | ON | FP16 SR5 | 20,500.9949 | 103.9990 | 256 | 3.4081 | 0 |
| Natural MTP3 | 256 | ON | FP8 SR5 — raw, quality failed† | 12,599.4779† | 85.6619† | 256 | 2.3517 | 0 |
| Natural MTP3 | 256 | ON | INT8 SR5 | 19,387.1414 | 97.2393 | 256 | 3.4030 | 0 |
| Natural MTP3 | 512 | ON | FP32 | 24,480.3667 | 59.8750 | 512 | 3.4211 | 0 |
| Natural MTP3 | 512 | ON | BF16 | 27,466.0912 | 68.4745 | 512 | 3.4140 | 0 |
| Natural MTP3 | 512 | ON | FP16 SR5 | 26,190.7631 | 65.3190 | 512 | 3.4156 | 0 |
| Natural MTP3 | 512 | ON | FP8 SR5 — raw, quality failed† | 16,610.3360† | 54.2818† | 512 | 2.4252 | 0 |
| Natural MTP3 | 512 | ON | INT8 SR5 | 24,049.9214 | 59.4198 | 512 | 3.4227 | 0 |
| Standard decoding | 256 | OFF | FP32 | 12,259.1275 | 48.3083 | 256 | — | 0 |
| Natural MTP3 | 256 | OFF | FP32 | 10,090.3307 | 65.4980 | 217 | 3.3919 | 0 |
| Natural MTP3 | 512 | OFF | FP32 | 11,348.3404 | 64.3266 | 216 | 3.4098 | 0 |

**Pinned environment**

- vLLM source: `927e98f31cc9f6bfafdb976ee2884b111446f371`.
- Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4`, revision `ff433f5493e25d631c9f12b5d55c674229923d02`.
- Dataset: `openai/gsm8k`, `main`, test split, revision `740312add88f781978c0658806c59bc2815b9866`.
- Runtime: Torch `2.14.0+cu130`, CUDA `13.0`, released FlashInfer `0.7.2.post1`, with no provider patches.
- GPU: NVIDIA GB300, driver `580.159.03`, power limit `1400 W`.
- Container: `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:544c00bd3e2efe2eb36bbfb22d926d43b85427611338187d99c5fb3f61dd456d`.

**Common configuration**

Set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` and `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. Use one fresh process per cell and one persistent FlashInfer tuning cache.
The runtime set `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1`.
The FP32 STP OFF reference ran first. ON formats ran in FP32, BF16, FP16, FP8, INT8 order for STP256, MTP256, then MTP512.
The FP32 OFF MTP references completed the original 18 runs.
The subsequent INT8 runs disabled SR and used STP256, MTP256, then MTP512 order.
Use these LLM settings with the pinned model and revision:

```python
common = dict(
    tensor_parallel_size=1, dtype="bfloat16", seed=0,
    mamba_backend="flashinfer", mamba_cache_dtype="bfloat16",
    mamba_cache_mode="none", enable_prefix_caching=False,
    enforce_eager=False, gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,
    kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3", replayssm_buffer_len=16,
    kernel_config={"enable_flashinfer_autotune": True},
    trust_remote_code=True, disable_log_stats=False,
)
```

Set `max_num_seqs` to the requested batch. Set `use_replayssm=True` for ON and `False` for the FP32 OFF references.

| Format | `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype` | `replayssm_state_dtype` | `enable_mamba_cache_stochastic_rounding` | `mamba_cache_philox_rounds` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| FP32 | `float32` | `auto` | `False` | 0 |
| BF16 | `bfloat16` | `auto` | `False` | 0 |
| FP16 SR5 | `float16` | `auto` | `True` | 5 |
| FP8 SR5 | `auto` | `fp8` | `True` | 5 |
| INT8 SR5 | `auto` | `int8` | `True` | 5 |
| INT8, SR off | `auto` | `int8` | `False` | 0 |

**Workload and timing**

- Standard: batch 256, `max_model_len=1256`, `enable_chunked_prefill=False`, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, and one 128-token warmup generation.
- Standard prompt: `My cat wrote all this CUDA code for a new language model and`, repeated across the batch.
- MTP: batch 256 or 512, `max_model_len=2048`, chunked prefill enabled, and `speculative_config={"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}`.
- MTP prompts: the first B pinned GSM8K test questions, with `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False}`.
- MTP warmup: repeated full-batch 256-token generations for at least 30 seconds.
- MTP graph capture: `sizes=(1,2,4,8,16,24,32,48,64,96,128,192,256,384,512)`. Use `sorted({4*min(n,batch) for n in sizes})` and maximum capture size `4*batch`.
- Throughput sampling: `n=1`, `temperature=0`, `seed=0`, `ignore_eos=True`, and equal minimum/maximum output counts of 1,000 or 256.
- Synchronize CUDA before and after timed generation. Calculate output TPS as `batch * output_tokens / elapsed_seconds`.
- Accuracy sampling: `n=1`, `temperature=0`, `seed=0`, `ignore_eos=False`, `max_tokens=1024`. Process all test questions in chunks of at most 256.

The [pinned paper scripts](https://github.com/Johnny-Liou/ReplaySSM/tree/73a9592e9d8a2268620e8883a82f5cec7442ed36/benchmarks/replayssm) define the original workloads.
They lack the complete current precision controls, so the settings above describe this experiment's adaptation.
The [measured-source checkpoint documentation](https://github.com/askliar/vllm/blob/927e98f31cc9f6bfafdb976ee2884b111446f371/docs/features/automatic_prefix_caching.md#shared-8-bit-replayssm-checkpoints) documents the options used for these measurements.
The harness retained commands, executed workload copies, worker proofs, timing records, and per-question outputs for every relevant run.

</details>

## Validation

Current rebase checks at `911ffe1d78cbb31b618a87fd2911fa6b57fd4597`:

- Focused CPU checks: **32 passed, 21 CUDA skips, 600 deselected**.
- Changed-file AST, Ruff, formatting, diff checks, and applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy.
- The rebase applied without conflicts. `git range-diff` confirms the feature patch is unchanged.
- No GPU, model-quality, or throughput run was repeated for this update.


Prior validation at `927e98f31cc9f6bfafdb976ee2884b111446f371` (shared diff: 19 files, +794/−38):

- Focused CPU checks: **32 passed, 21 CUDA skips, 597 deselected**. These checks cover configuration, cache records, and lifecycle contracts.
- Changed Python files passed AST parsing, Ruff, formatting, and diff checks.
- Existing ReplaySSM CI selects shared GPU arithmetic/cache cases and real FP8/INT8 prefix-cache E2E cases.
- The earlier local check skipped CUDA tests. GB300 measurements cover the original 18 runs and five full-test evaluations, plus three INT8-no-SR runs and one full-test evaluation.
- FP8 SR5 failed the quality comparison. Dedicated GPU arithmetic and prefix-cache coverage remain outstanding.
- The native conversion/default-RNG diagnostic passed within its stated limits. It does not replace full SSM or model validation.

Historical evidence only: the October 28 GB10 Bolt/LiLiCorr matrix recorded 76.3966 BF16, 79.7057 FP8 SR5, and 80.2785 INT8 decode TPS/user.
It used the older combined source, synthetic AL4.3, subset-72 routing, B1/T8, 32K input, 4K output, and five measured requests per mode.
The earlier eight-question natural-acceptance GSM8K checks scored 7/8 for each shared format. This small sample does not establish quality parity.
These older measurements do not establish correctness for the updated branch or isolate this PR's effect.

GPU test entry points remain in `tests/kernels/mamba/test_ssu_dispatch.py`.
Model cases remain in `tests/v1/e2e/test_replayssm_decode.py`.

## Details

The implementation extends the merged ReplaySSM five-state cache with a matching scale page for the quantized SSM payload.
The three replay rings and convolution cache retain their existing types.
Prefill uses floating-point working state and encodes final or prefix-boundary checkpoints before publication.
The implementation rejects malformed records that omit scales.
The merged ReplaySSM exporter, ring-shape helpers, and extensible-cache warmup remain in use.

This is the shared portion of the requested split, not a competing implementation of #52962.
The child PR contains the separate checkpoint layout, native kernels, and separate-only request-ordering changes.
AI tools assisted implementation, review, validation, and this description.

---

- [x] AI tools assisted creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Shared FlashInfer integration excludes the separate native kernels.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** The FP8 SR5 quality regression remains open. Dedicated GPU arithmetic and prefix-cache coverage remain outstanding.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Independent review, static checks, and signed-off commits completed. This description discloses AI assistance.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Scope, dependencies, validation revisions, and historical evidence are explicit.
</details>

The runtime set `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1`.

The subsequent INT8 runs disabled SR and used STP256, MTP256, then MTP512 order.

The [pinned paper scripts](https://github.com/Johnny-Liou/ReplaySSM/tree/73a9592e9d8a2268620e8883a82f5cec7442ed36/benchmarks/replayssm) define the original workloads.

- The native conversion/default-RNG diagnostic passed within its stated limits. It does not replace full SSM or model validation.

It used the older combined source, synthetic AL4.3, subset-72 routing, B1/T8, 32K input, 4K output, and five measured requests per mode.
The earlier eight-question natural-acceptance GSM8K checks scored 7/8 for each shared format. This small sample does not establish quality parity.
These older measurements do not establish correctness for the updated branch or isolate this PR's effect.

GPU test entry points remain in `tests/kernels/mamba/test_ssu_dispatch.py`.
Model cases remain in `tests/v1/e2e/test_replayssm_decode.py`.

## Details

The implementation extends the merged ReplaySSM five-state cache with a matching scale page for the quantized SSM payload.
The three replay rings and convolution cache retain their existing types.
Prefill uses floating-point working state and encodes final or prefix-boundary checkpoints before publication.
The implementation rejects malformed records that omit scales.
The merged ReplaySSM exporter, ring-shape helpers, and extensible-cache warmup remain in use.

This is the shared portion of the requested split, not a competing implementation of #52962.
The child PR contains the separate checkpoint layout, native kernels, and separate-only request-ordering changes.

+def _bytes(value):
+    return value.contiguous().view(torch.uint8).cpu()
+
+
+def _encode_rows(value, dtype):
+    value = value.float().cpu()
+    qmax = 127 if dtype == torch.int8 else 448
+    amax = value.abs().amax(-1)
+    multiplier = torch.where(amax == 0, 1.0, qmax / amax)
+    scaled = value * multiplier[..., None]
+    if dtype == torch.int8:
+        scaled = scaled.round()
+    return scaled.to(dtype), multiplier.reciprocal()
+
+
+def _assert_rows(value, payload, scale):
+    expected_payload, expected_scale = _encode_rows(value, payload.dtype)
+    assert torch.equal(_bytes(payload), _bytes(expected_payload))
+    torch.testing.assert_close(scale.cpu(), expected_scale, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def _source(dtype):
+    qmax = 127 if dtype == torch.int8 else 448
+    value = torch.ones(3, 16, 64, 128)
+    value[..., -1] = qmax
+    factors = torch.exp2(torch.arange(16 * 64).reshape(16, 64) % 3 - 2)
+    return value * factors[None, ..., None], factors

+    payload, scale = payload_pages[::2], scale_pages[::2]

+"""Prefill conversion for FlashInfer shared quantized checkpoints."""

+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton

+@triton.jit
+def _quantize_checkpoint(
+    source,
+    state,
+    scales,
+    destinations,
+    sources,
+    source_stride,
+    state_stride,
+    scale_stride,
+    ROWS: tl.constexpr,
+    N: tl.constexpr,
+    QMAX: tl.constexpr,
+    HAS_SOURCES: tl.constexpr,
+    INT8: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    batch, row = tl.program_id(0), tl.program_id(1)
+    dst = tl.load(destinations + batch).to(tl.int64)
+    if dst <= 0:
+        return
+    src = tl.load(sources + batch).to(tl.int64) if HAS_SOURCES else batch
+    cols = tl.arange(0, N)
+    value = tl.load(source + src * source_stride + row * N + cols).to(tl.float32)
+    amax = tl.max(tl.abs(value), axis=0)

+            constraints="=r,f",

+            dtype=tl.int32,
+            is_pure=True,
+            pack=1,

+    tl.store(state + dst * state_stride + row * N + cols, quantized)
+    tl.store(scales + dst * scale_stride + row, 1.0 / encode)
